audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Skill / Sion / Sion / Skill / Skill / Sion / Sion, which disagrees with the packet and with the already-audited mirror at four stages.
audit.why: packet.levelChart and the mirror both lock Sion / Skill / Sion / Sion / Aurora / Sion / Sion, and the entry's own whys[0] (no escape at level 1) and whys[4] (her R breaks your charge line) already argue that shape.
audit.corrected: Level 1 to Sion, Level 2 to Skill, Levels 4-5 to Sion, Level 6 to Aurora — proposed as matched full/content pairs, with phases[0].why and phases[4].why rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike said 'her R reposition resets her kite angle' without naming Between Worlds or describing what it actually leaves behind.
audit.why: Between Worlds (R, 140/120/100s) leaps her out, shockwaves and slows, then creates an area she can teleport across from side to side. The teleport, not the leap, is what makes your charge whiff — which is exactly what the mirror recorded.
audit.corrected: spikes[2], whys[4], phases[4].why and wants.foe[2] now name Between Worlds and its rift teleport.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry calls Aurora's escape 'Twofold Hex (E)' and tracks it as the blink across both layers — tldr, winCon, focus, dosFull, breakdown.cooldowns, report[5], wants.you[0] and wants.foe[0].
audit.why: Twofold Hex is her Q: a 900-range curse missile on 9/8.5/8/7.5/7s that she recasts to drag the curses back through you. It is not a blink and it is not her E. Her E is The Weirding (15/14/13/12/11s, 825 range), a blast that slows and then hops her backward; her W is Across the Veil (22s), the leap into invisibility. Tracking the wrong ability means tracking the wrong cooldown before every commit.
audit.corrected: Every 'escape' reference retargeted to The Weirding with its 15s rank-1 cooldown; Twofold Hex restated as the curse-and-recall poke in wants.foe[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: No Grievous Wounds line despite her passive healing off every spell she lands.
audit.why: Spirit Abjuration exorcises spirits from damaged enemies that follow her and heal her — in the extended brawls this entry tells you to force, that healing is the deciding term.
audit.corrected: late now pairs the 'force extended brawls' instruction with the anti-heal buy.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 belong to Sion on cooldown math alone — Twofold Hex sits on a meaningful timer, and every time it is down you run the full pattern: E armor-shred, charged Q stun, brawl with W-shield detonating mid-trade. When Twofold Hex is up, give nothing: back to the wave, freeze, and make her walk to you. At level 6 the dynamic shifts temporarily — Aurora's R is a repositioning tool that breaks Unstoppable Onslaught's tracking angle, so she can blink sideways out of your R path and punish the cooldown. Treat level 6 as a mutual standoff and wait for her R to be committed elsewhere before re-engaging.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 belong to Sion on cooldown math alone — The Weirding is 15s at rank 1, and every time it is down you run the full pattern: Roar of the Slayer's armour shred, charged Q stun, brawl with Soul Furnace detonating mid-trade. When the hop is up, give nothing: back to the wave, freeze, and make her walk to you. At level 6 the dynamic shifts temporarily — Between Worlds leaps her sideways and leaves a rift she teleports across, so she slips your R path and punishes the 140s cooldown. Treat level 6 as a mutual standoff and wait for it to be spent elsewhere before re-engaging.

edits.before: First item Heartsteel is where Sion reasserts dominance for the remainder of the game — his HP passive begins compounding in earnest, Soul Furnace shield value climbs with every stack, and Aurora's burst numbers stop keeping pace with his bulk. Force extended brawls on Twofold Hex's cooldown and let the zombie passive threaten damage even if she kills you; she cannot safely ignore a reanimated Sion ramming into her. In a truly even game she remains a burst threat with her full AP build, so never commit Unstoppable Onslaught into a visible R — bait her R first, then close.
edits.after: First item Heartsteel is where Sion reasserts dominance for the remainder of the game — his HP passive begins compounding in earnest, Soul Furnace shield value climbs with every stack, and Aurora's burst stops keeping pace with his bulk. Force extended brawls on The Weirding's cooldown with Grievous Wounds already bought, or Spirit Abjuration's spirits refund everything you chip; and let the zombie passive threaten her even if she kills you. She stays a burst threat, so never commit Unstoppable Onslaught into an uncast Between Worlds — bait it first, then close.

notes: The load-bearing error here is a slot mix-up repeated across both layers: 'Twofold Hex (E)' as Aurora's escape blink. Twofold Hex is her Q curse missile (9s); the hop is The Weirding (E, 15s) and the invisibility leap is Across the Veil (W, 22s). A reader tracking a 9s Q as the dodge window will commit into a live 15s hop. Chart also flipped to the packet and mirror shape as matched pairs.
